scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Bygdedans is identified as the oldest and most distinctive of Norwegian folk dances, surviving primarily in isolated farming communities.
While coastal and urban areas shifted toward newer styles like Gammaldans following the introduction of the accordion, these village dances maintained their ancient musical roots.
on_screen: Map: Norway · Europe

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Bygdedans serves as a regional marker of identity.
It represents a traditional form of social interaction that predates the more standardized European partner dances that arrived later.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance typically follows a three-part sequence: the figuring part, the free dancing part (lausdans), and the closed hold part (samdans).
The two main forms are the gangar (walking dance in 2/4 or 3/8) and the springar (running dance in 3/4), which vary in intensity and tempo.
Watch for Lausdans, Samdans.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Couples moving through figuring, free dancing, and closed hold.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The Hardanger fiddle is the primary instrument for Bygdedans.
The music is considered among the oldest living traditions in Norway.
Listen for the Hardanger fiddle.
The pulse is 2/4, 3/8, or 3/4.

The sound is dominated by the Hardanger fiddle's sympathetic strings, creating a drone-like resonance. The rhythm is characterized by asymmetrical pulses that vary by valley, creating a driving but non-standard 3/4 or 2/4 feel.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Significant variants include the Telemark and Setesdal gangar, the Valdres springar, and the western 'rull' or 'rudl'.
Bygdedans is the ancestor to or contemporary of several other Norwegian forms.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Bygdedans is parent of Gangar: One of the two basic forms of Bygdedans.
Bygdedans is parent of Springar: One of the two basic forms of Bygdedans.
Bygdedans is child of Halling: An athletic, mostly male dance seen as an heir to the gangar.
Bygdedans is influence of Gammaldans: The newer popular dance style that replaced Bygdedans in urban areas.

scenes.title: Common mistakes and what to avoid
narration: Avoid applying a standard, even 3/4 waltz beat to the asymmetrical Springar rhythms.
on_screen: Side-by-side: source-supported correction

Options card: Seated or supported option: Focus on the rhythmic hand-clapping of the asymmetrical 3/4 pulses (Telemark vs Valdres styles). · For children: A 'follow the leader' game for the figuring part, transitioning to 'freeze dance' during the lausdans.
options: Seated or supported option: Focus on the rhythmic hand-clapping of the asymmetrical 3/4 pulses (Telemark vs Valdres styles).
For children: A 'follow the leader' game for the figuring part, transitioning to 'freeze dance' during the lausdans.
